stem: Which of the following functions has a maximum value?
solution: A quadratic function has a maximum value only when its graph is a parabola that opens downward, which happens when the coefficient of \(x^{2}\) is negative.
In \(f(x) = -3x^{2} + 2x\) the coefficient of \(x^{2}\) is \(-3\), so this function has a maximum.
The other quadratics open upward (minimum only), and \(3^{x}\) keeps increasing without bound.

explanation.A: Incorrect. The coefficient of \(x^{2}\) is positive, so the parabola opens upward and has a minimum, not a maximum.
explanation.B: Correct. The negative coefficient \(-3\) makes the parabola open downward, so it has a highest point.
explanation.C: Incorrect. \((x - 3)^{2}\) is never negative and opens upward; its smallest value is \(0\), but it has no largest value.
explanation.D: Incorrect. An exponential function with base \(3\) increases without limit, so it has no maximum value.
